change: The Web viewer now treats selection of the same publication generation and media elements as a no-op, retains its media elements and reusable audio output across supported rebinds, rejects callbacks that no longer match the selected publication, and permits at most one explicit same-publication video recovery attempt. SDK subscription failure is surfaced only for the selected track SID. Sender-muted and hidden-tab states are distinguished without automatic retry. If a publication disappears or is replaced while its session identity cannot be confirmed, the viewer ends the selection and requires an explicit new choice.

checks.name: focused_viewer_tests
checks.detail: 9 files, 44 tests; includes 100 repeated same-generation selections, stable binding counts, replaced publication fail-closed behavior, retry bounds, stale A-to-B callbacks, in-generation track replacement observation, SDK failure SID filtering, sender-muted state and shared-player structure.

checks.name: web_production_build
checks.detail: VITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://localhost:4810 npm run build passed vue-tsc and Vite. Existing ineffective LiveKit dynamic-import and >500 kB chunk warnings remain.

checks.detail: No real browser/device run captured actual full, mini, resize, pin, autoplay, audio-output, background/static video or 100-cycle memory behavior.

checks.name: pixel_screenshot_diff
checks.detail: This packet changed viewer lifecycle behavior and did not capture real browser screenshots or compare rendered pixels.

limitation: The current Web LiveKit adapter does not carry the shared v1 session descriptor. Same-generation recovery is therefore bounded to the still-present SDK publication object; disappearance or replacement fails closed. Tests do not prove audible output, first-frame latency, hidden-tab behavior on a browser, SFU recovery, device compatibility or long-run memory stability. No SDK keyframe/PLI API was introduced.
